I recall a chilly morning in early March when I was just 14 years old. I had been tasked with cooking breakfast for my family on a particularly busy weekday. The menu was simple: scrambled eggs, toast, and a side of bacon. It had been my first attempt at cooking for them, and I was eager to impress.

In my excitement, I neglected to check if the bacon had been thawed before placing it in the pan. As the bacon sizzled, I noticed it was still frozen solid, but I thought it would be okay. I continued to cook it, hoping for the best. The bacon started to curl and crackle, but I didn't pay it much mind, focused instead on the eggs and the toast.

When it was time to serve, I noticed the bacon was still uncooked. My stomach churned
